page.layout: Top: running head with page number at upper right. Above the text, a four-row table of three columns (German, German, Latin). Below it, one block of running text in roman type, with a margin note at the right. Then a centred title, and a black-letter Dutch prayer in one paragraph. Below the prayer, a single letter "G" at the right.

main_text.p: In aliis quidem & remotioribus earun-dem ad Septentrionem regionum locis, lin-guam à communi Germanicâ multùm va-riare puto. nam, ut Olaus Magnus scribit, veterum dominorum montes vocant Hor-nillabuck, Diabolum Trol, & fluvium quen-dam, Trolheta, id est, diaboli verticem vel caput. het[?] puto eis caput est: & cetum ingen-tem troluual.

Septentrionales & maritimi Germani,Septentrionales Germani intellectu difficiles. quos inferiores vocamus, smutant int: & b inf: & 3 quoque in t. Quare à superio-ribus Germanis non facilè intelligi possunt, Munsterus.

p.bl: Onse vayer/ Die[?] ghey seit in den[?] hemel: geheilicht sey uwen naem: wu reyck ons toecoem: uwen wil geschie uperden als in den hemel: geeft ons heuyen ons daghe-lichs broot/ ende vergeeft ons onse schult/ als wey vergeven onse sculdenaers: ende enleyt ons niet in becoringhe/ sond verloest ons van allen quaden. Amen.

page.notes: Running head read as "DIVERSIS." with a doubtful long-s-like letter; the page number 49 is printed top right. Table: "Dicke" has a decorative first letter, read as D with [?]. "het" in "het puto" is doubtful. The Dutch prayer is set in black letter; "Die", "den", "wu" and "het" are doubtful readings. The margin note is set in small type and spans three lines beside "Germani,"; its hyphenation is not clear from the scan, so its words are written whole. A dark blot over "Hornillabuck" hides part of the "b". No catchword or signature.
